An employee adequately accounts to their employer by providing a statement of expense, account book, diary, or similar record with each expense entered at or near the time incurred, along with documentary evidence such as receipts
An accountable plan requires the employee to return any excess reimbursement or allowance within a reasonable period of time
An arrangement is not treated as a reimbursement or other expense allowance arrangement if it does not require the employee to substantiate expenses to the payor
An arrangement is not treated as a reimbursement or other expense allowance arrangement if it provides the employee the right to retain any amount in excess of substantiated expenses

verdicts.why: 26 CFR 1.62-2(c)(1) states arrangement must meet requirements of business connection, substantiation, and returning excess amounts.
Sources define business connection requirement but not as limited to deductible expenses; they mention some reimbursed expenses may be nondeductible.
IRS Pub 463 p. 43 describes adequate accounting as providing statement, account book, diary with each expense entered at or near time incurred, plus documentary evidence.
26 CFR 1.62-2(f) and IRS Pub 463 p. 42 address returning excess reimbursements within reasonable period for accountable plans.
26 U.S.C. § 62(c)(1) states arrangement not treated as reimbursement arrangement if doesn't require substantiation of expenses.
26 U.S.C. § 62(c)(2) states arrangement not treated as reimbursement arrangement if provides right to retain excess amounts.
